cause: **Single-change → full-verify churn.** Consecutive attempts burn steps on one-line edits, whole-file rewrites (once byte-identical), and full test-plus-probe runs after each. It should batch related changes and verify once, and never re-write a file it just read unchanged.
subject: Prompt now batches edits and verifies once.
description: I added one bullet to jig's system prompt in `src/prompt.ts`, between the "keep changes focused" and "Verify your work" bullets. It tells the model to batch related edits and verify once rather than after each one, to re-run only the failing check after a fix, and not to write a file's same content back. The first two clauses target the edit→full-test churn loop; the last targets the byte-identical whole-file rewrites. It's general (no task, file or test named), adds ~30 words to the stable, cacheable prompt prefix, and doesn't weaken verification — it just makes it happen once, at the right time. The suite shows only the 7 pre-existing sandbox/`ps` failures and no new ones; the prompt/`--tools` assertions in `test/tools.test.ts` still pass.

verdict.reason: no better on the training tasks (+7 points, ahead in 53% of resamples, cost ×0.92)
